requirements.statement: The Ask surface answers natural-language questions about personal context through the Context Broker with source links and explanation controls (§7.2, FR-090).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The Commitments surface shows open commitments, due dates, overdue projections, related people and sources, resolution evidence, and uncertain or contested commitments (§7.3, FR-090).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The Weekly Review compares stated priorities with calendar allocation, open commitments with completed resolutions, decisions with outcomes where available, planned with observed spending where available, and reports material changes (§7.5, §39).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Behavioral observations require multiple supporting episodes, counterexample search, an observation window, confidence, and a review or expiry date, and a single event never creates a stable personality claim (FR-094, §39).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The Memory Inspector shows current belief, historical timeline, original evidence, claims and asserting actors, inferences, conflicts, resolution assertions, connected memory threads, access history, and registry and extractor versions (§7.6, FR-090).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The Memory Inbox presents batched review cards that group related uncertainty and state why each matters and what will change (§7.7, §37.4, FR-090).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The Permissions and Integrations surface lets the user inspect and change connected sources, read and write scopes, domain sensitivity, plugin capabilities, attention budgets, data retention, and export and deletion (§7.8).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The user has separate Correct, Changed, Confirm, Reject, Keep uncertain, Suppress, Archive, Delete, Merge, and Split actions backed by separate API semantics, never a single edit-memory action (FR-091, §37.3, §35.11, §35.12).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Every material personal statement exposes a Why?/Sources action opening the accepted belief or overlay assertion, claiming actor, source excerpt, effective time, confidence and conflict status, and derivation path if inferred (FR-092, §37.1).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The UI visibly distinguishes confirmed, reported, inferred, contested, pending owner assertion, scheduled/planned, and resolved memory without relying on color alone (§37.2, §41 Accessibility).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: The UI makes clear whether Uai observed, suggested, drafted, requested approval, executed, or received confirmation of execution (§37.8).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Core views are keyboard navigable and usable with screen readers (§41 Accessibility).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: A memory thread view presents current projection, timeline, plans and expected outcomes, actual events, resolution links, open uncertainties, and related people, documents, and decisions (§37.5).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Language models may propose semantic updates but cannot commit accepted memory except through a Belief Transaction (FR-040, §19.1).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Belief Transaction commit is atomic and idempotent (FR-041, §35.5).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Local policy ports EvaluateMemoryWrite, EvaluateMemoryRead, and EvaluateMemoryAction are implemented behind stable interfaces, evaluated before commit, read, or action, and Uai functions fully without Cordum (FR-042, §29.3, §29.4).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Admission supports SOURCE_ONLY, INDEX_ONLY, AUTO_CLAIM, AUTO_ACCEPT, AUTO_PROVISIONAL, BATCH_REVIEW, and JUST_IN_TIME modes, with AUTO_ACCEPT only when all §19.2 conditions hold (FR-044).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Proactive clarification obeys configurable attention budgets defaulting to at most three cards per owner per day, at most one per sensitivity scope per day, and no repeat of an unresolved question within seven days absent material new evidence, with policy inputs and decision reason logged (FR-045, §19.3, §19.4).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Learned approval rules become active only after explicit user approval and remain inspectable, reversible, and scoped (§19.5).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Triage routes every source item through deterministic Tier-0 parsing and a Tier-1 decision (SOURCE_ONLY, INDEX_ONLY, ENTITY_EXTRACTION, FULL_EXTRACTION, DEFER_UNTIL_RELEVANT) with a recorded routing reason before any deep extraction (§20.1-§20.5).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Every extraction run records model/provider, prompt version, registry release, normalization version, entity-resolver and temporal-resolver versions, run timestamp, cost, and latency, and re-extraction creates new claims without mutating old ones (§22.1).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.

requirements.statement: Shadow re-extraction and registry evaluation change no production state and produce instance-match, slot-collision, proposition, belief-status, resolution, projection, and cost/latency diffs (§22.2, §43.5).

review.detail: Mapped implementation choices and contract tests retain this requirement. Passing tests and an ADR do not replace independent criterion verification.
